claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar-colony microstructure with numerous internal boundaries.
Cryogenic thermal cycling can introduce a controlled amount of lattice distortion in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Cryogenic thermal cycling alters dislocation dynamics through the introduced lattice distortion.
Internal boundaries can act as microcrack-initiation or propagation sites during deformation of dual-phase high-entropy alloys.
Cryogenic-thermal-cycling-induced changes in dislocation dynamics can reduce microcracking at internal boundaries.
Reduced microcracking at internal boundaries can enhance room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cryogenic thermal cycling refines the alloy microstructure.
Cryogenic-thermal-cycling-induced lattice distortion increases lattice friction.
Microstructural refinement and increased lattice friction maintain or increase tensile strength.
Cryogenic thermal cycling improves both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility relative to an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
The effectiveness of cryogenic thermal cycling depends on alloy composition.
The effectiveness of cryogenic thermal cycling depends on the extent of lattice distortion introduced.
The effectiveness of cryogenic thermal cycling depends on the number of thermal cycles.
